questions.prompt: What is a safe retry policy for a rate-limited or failing dependency?
options: Retry immediately forever until the request succeeds.
Retry every state-changing request regardless of idempotency.
Ignore Retry-After and increase concurrent attempts after each failure.
Use finite timeouts, bounded retries with backoff/jitter, and retry only when the operation semantics permit it.
questions.answer_key: Use finite timeouts, bounded retries with backoff/jitter, and retry only when the operation semantics permit it.
questions.explanation: Use finite timeouts, bounded retries with backoff/jitter, and retry only when the operation semantics permit it. This is especially relevant to “Retry-After and Backoff” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Retry-After and Backoff”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Simulate persistent failure and confirm timeouts, retry limits, and rate-limit signals work.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
questions.answer_key: Simulate persistent failure and confirm timeouts, retry limits, and rate-limit signals work.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Retry-After and Backoff”?
options: The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
Retries are unbounded, timeouts absent, or rate limits are not observable.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
questions.answer_key: Retries are unbounded, timeouts absent, or rate limits are not observable.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
